template_en: [ipa] is more open and centralized than the full stressed /a/ (pretonic a/o).

The template's blanket 'always reduces' contradicts this for a (and very likely for o by the parallel akanye rule). Flagging for Dann; not proposing new wording.

template_en: [ipa] is the most reduced vowel in Russian; it should sound neutral and centralized (a/o/ya/ye/e, remote and post-stress).
quote: [U]: 'produced with relatively relaxed articulators...and an open resonator' (p.108). [H]: 'like the pronunciation of the -i- in the English word bit...centralizes' (p.112).
note: Two different allophones ([U] for a/o, [H] for ya/ye/e) are both described in neutral/centralized terms within the cited range; reasonable single paraphrase.

note: Grayson's example word is 'gli', not 'figlio' (figlio contains gli); reasonable paraphrase, page correct.
